subject: New paper using Stan to test for discrimination

messages.author: f0ce474d9924d57a
messages.subject: New paper using Stan to test for discrimination
parts: We recently used Stan to fit a statistical model which tests for discrimination. We describe the work in this paper: https://5harad.com/papers/fast-threshold-test.pdf. We found that we were able to accelerate inference by several orders of magnitude by using a class of distributions that we are calling discriminant distributions. We would welcome any feedback on the distribution, the model, or the paper in general!

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] New paper using Stan to test for discrimination
parts: Yes, it's the distribution of p(Y|X) where X is drawn from a two-component normal mixture with Y denoting component membership. p(Y|X) is of course simple to compute but we weren't sure anyone had ever used its distribution like this before (in particular, to approximate a beta or logit-normal for computational speedups).

messages.author: f0ce474d9924d57a
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] New paper using Stan to test for discrimination
parts: Thanks! Well, you start with 5 parameters in the original formulation, but the actual family we consider has only 2 (briefly, you lose one parameter because you restrict the two normals to have equal variances so that p(Y|X) is monotonic in X; then you lose another two because you can show that all that matters for the distribution of p(Y|X) is the difference in the means divided by the standard deviation. In the end the distribution is parameterized by the probability of being in the positive class and the separation between the two classes).
